content.value_statement: Cold outreach often sounds generic, pushy, or too long. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft concise emails, subject lines, and follow-ups.
actual_capabilities: Drafts first-touch cold emails from audience, offer, proof, and desired outcome.
Creates short subject line options for B2B outreach.
Builds 3-5 touch follow-up sequences with changing angles and breakup emails.
Reviews existing cold emails for weak personalization, jargon, length, and CTA friction.
Adapts tone for executives, managers, and technical buyers.
Uses benchmark and framework references to explain recommendations.
limitations: Does not send emails, scrape prospects, enrich leads, or connect to email tools.
Does not verify deliverability, legal compliance, or current spam rule changes.
Requires accurate product, audience, proof, and targeting details for strong output.
Best suited for B2B cold outreach, not lifecycle or nurture campaigns.

use_cases.title: Start a Prospecting Campaign
use_cases.description: Draft concise first-touch emails with subject lines, personalization hooks, proof points, and low-friction CTAs.

use_cases.title: Rewrite Low-Reply Outreach
use_cases.description: Diagnose a weak cold email and replace generic copy with sharper, more relevant messaging.

use_cases.title: Build Follow-Up Sequences
use_cases.description: Create multi-touch sequences that rotate value, proof, insight, and a respectful breakup email.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a First Email
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new cold outreach message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a cold email to [role] at [company type]. We sell [product] that solves [problem]. Use this proof: [proof]. Give three subject lines and two email options.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Email
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for reviewing and rewriting current copy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this cold email for clarity, personalization, tone, subject line, and CTA. Then rewrite it in under 100 words: [paste email].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Follow-Up Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a full outbound sequence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 5-touch cold email sequence for [persona] about [offer]. Rotate angles across proof, insight, resource, and breakup. Include timing and subject lines.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Segment Variations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for segmented campaign planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design cold email variations for [segment A], [segment B], and [segment C]. For each segment, choose a research signal, problem hook, proof point, CTA, and subject line.

output_examples.input: Write to VP Marketing at B2B SaaS companies about a content analytics platform with 3x pipeline attribution proof.
output_examples.output:
Subject: content attribution

Noticed many B2B teams can name their top posts, but not the posts creating pipeline. We help marketing teams connect content to revenue without manual reporting. Customers usually see 3x more content-attributed revenue within 90 days. Worth a look?

output_examples.input: Review an email that opens with 'I hope this email finds you well' and asks for a 30-minute demo.
output_examples.output: The opening is filler, the value is too vague, and the CTA asks for too much too soon. A stronger version should lead with the prospect's problem, use one proof point, and ask for a simple reply.

output_examples.input: Create follow-ups after a first email about HR software receives no reply.
output_examples.output: The sequence should wait three days, then add a new angle. Follow-ups can rotate through a hiring bottleneck insight, a customer proof point, a useful resource, and a final breakup note.

best_practices: Connect every personalization detail to the prospect's likely business problem.
Use one clear CTA that can be answered with a short reply.
Keep emails short, specific, and honest about the sender and offer.
anti_patterns: Using fake Re: or Fwd: subject lines to imply an existing conversation.
Sending the same template with only a name or company merge tag changed.
Using guilt, pressure, or repeated follow-ups after a breakup email.

faq.question: Can this skill send email campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It only drafts, reviews, and structures copy. It does not send messages or connect to mail platforms.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best emails?
faq.answer: Provide the target role, company type, offer, business problem, proof point, and desired next step.

faq.question: Does it handle follow-up emails?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create 3-5 touch sequences with timing, changing angles, and a final breakup email.

faq.question: Can it write for technical buyers?
faq.answer: Yes. It adapts tone for technical audiences with precise language, less hype, and clear proof.

faq.question: Does it cover legal compliance?
faq.answer: It can remind users to follow applicable laws, but it is not legal advice. Verify consent, unsubscribe, and regional requirements.

faq.question: How is cold email different from lifecycle email?
faq.answer: Cold email is unsolicited outreach to new prospects. Lifecycle email targets opted-in users, customers, or existing leads.
